questions.q: What problem does an allocation solve that a single formula recurring journal does not?
options: Calculating one amount for one pair of accounts
Posting a journal automatically without validation
Distributing one pool of cost or revenue across many targets at once, based on usage
Importing journals from a spreadsheet
questions.explain: Allocations spread a single pool across many destinations proportionally, unlike a formula journal calculating one amount for one relationship.

questions.q: What is the core allocation formula?
options: Cost Pool divided by number of periods
Total Usage divided by Cost Pool
Usage Factor multiplied by Total Usage
Cost Pool multiplied by (Target's Usage Factor divided by Total Usage)
questions.explain: Each target's share is the cost pool times its usage factor divided by total usage across all targets.

questions.q: In the Solara Fixtures example, why does Sales receive $15,000 of the $60,000 facilities pool?
options: Because Sales has 30 of the 120 total employees (30/120 = 25% of $60,000)
Because Sales requested that specific amount
Because Sales has the most employees
Because the allocation is split evenly regardless of headcount
questions.explain: Sales has 30 of 120 total employees, so it receives 30/120, or 25%, of the $60,000 pool — $15,000.

questions.q: What does 'mass' in mass allocation emphasize?
options: That the allocation only works for large companies
That one rule definition can spread a pool across an entire range of targets, not just a few
That the allocation must use the Mass journal category
That it requires manual approval for every target
questions.explain: Mass allocation means one rule can sweep across a whole range or hierarchy of targets, scaling without rewriting the rule.

questions.q: What happens when a new cost center is added to the business, assuming it falls within an existing mass allocation rule's range?
options: The allocation rule must be completely rewritten
The allocation stops working until manually reconfigured
A new ledger must be created
It automatically falls into the range the rule already covers, with no rule change needed
questions.explain: Because mass allocation rules target a range or hierarchy, a new cost center within that range is covered automatically.
